newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia mulls state monopoly for caviar exports.
newsitem.headline: Russia mulls state monopoly for caviar exports.

text.p: Russia, worried by a wave of illegal black caviar sales, may reintroduce a state monopoly on exports of the famed delicacy, an official of the State Committee for Fishing said on Wednesday.

Interfax news agency quoted Vyacheslav Zilanov as saying a monopoly on sturgeon caviar exports from the Caspian Sea, such as exists in neighbouring Iran, another major exporter, would halt the "poaching outrage".

Zilanov said illegal caviar exports by poachers were three times greater than official export levels of the three former Soviet republics that border the Caspian Sea -- Russia, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan.
He said that his committee would present a draft law to the government reinstating the state monopoly.
In communist times all fishing firms had to sell caviar through Moscow, but after the break-up of the Soviet Union in 1991 the firms were allowed to export the black salty raw fish eggs directly.
He said Russia planned to export 60 tonnes of black caviar in 1997 against a total output of 100 tonnes. Russia has a quota to fish 1,500 tonnes of sturgeon in the Caspian in 1997.
Sturgeon catches have declined sharply in recent years in the landlocked Caspian Sea because of illegal fishing and increased oil production.
